notes: Page 2 also shows two minifigure assemblies (orange alien and a gray/black agent). Their parts aren't in the parts list, so no pieces were recorded for them.
Step 3 shows a STOP sticker applied to the white round sign. A sticker isn't a piece, so it isn't recorded.
The bar is shown standing in the axle hole of the base plate, so it has no piece beneath it to rest on.
Stack order from the bottom is b4, b5, b6, so the green light is on the bottom brick and the red light is on the top. I put the lights on the side studs of the matching bricks, as the page shows.

The page shows the bar's stop-ring end at the bottom of the post. The bar joins the stack underneath and the base plate holds the lower end. I assumed the bar passes into the plate's axle hole, as it did on page 2.
Page 4 starts the second model. The small picture at the top left shows the finished vehicle, so I did not record it.

The step 1 callout shows a ready-made sub-assembly: white tricycle top, gray chassis, wheels, and a clip at the back. I recorded it only as the single part lego-30187b. The clip and wheels look like part of that moulded piece, since no other parts match.
In step 2 the right-hand curved brick is already shown fitted, and the left one is being added. The callout says 2x, so I recorded both as placed on this page.
I could not tell exactly which port each curved brick attaches to. I recorded the attachment as a sideways join to the body, with the port left unnamed.
Step 3: the two white 1x4 studded bricks sit side by side on the studs of the body (b12). Their side studs face outward. They overhang the body at the front.
Step 4: one grille slope goes on each long side of the 2x4 stud area. I assumed the near slope sits on b15 and the far slope on b16. The page does not show exactly which studs each slope covers.

Step 5: the model is turned over and viewed from the other side. The two white curved bricks are rear wing pieces, one on each side of the rear clip area. I recorded the attachment as sideways joins to the body b12. The exact port is not visible.

Step 6: the trans-dark blue slope, trans-red slope and dark gray jumper plate sit on the studs of the white 1x4 bricks. I assumed the red slope is on b15 and the blue slope and jumper are on b16. The page does not show exactly which studs each one covers.

Step 7: the black 1x1 clip tile (b24) goes on the stud of the jumper plate b23. Both 2x Technic pin connectors (b25, b26) are placed on this page. One is already drawn in the left rear of the picture and the other is shown on its arrow.
I assumed the connectors join the side studs of the white 1x4 bricks. Which brick each one joins is a guess (b25 to b16, b26 to b15).

Step 8: the handlebars sit in the clip of b24. The blaster (b28) goes on the rear of the body, with a trans-orange round plate (b30) pushed onto its front end. The white 1x2 tile (b29) sits across the white bricks at the front-left.
Which exact studs the handlebar and blaster attach to is not fully clear. I recorded them as sideways joins.
Step 9: the sub-assembly (a cone on a pin with bar) is built 2x and each copy goes into one of the black pin connectors b25 and b26. The pairing of copy to connector is assumed.
The page also shows a sticker (black 'POLICE' label) going onto the white 1x2 tile b29. A sticker isn't a piece, so it isn't recorded.
The agent minifigure is shown seated on the vehicle. It is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded.
The warning icon at the bottom right is not a building step.
Page 9 starts the third model. The small picture at the top left shows the finished model, so I did not record it.
Step 1: the sub-assembly shown (black tube with a flat 2x2 stud plate on top) is the single moulded lego-4868b engine, so I recorded it as one part.

Step 2: I assumed the two brackets sit side by side on the 2x2 top of the engine. They are mirrored so their vertical faces point in opposite directions. A sticker (a black badge) goes on the engine side. A sticker isn't a piece, so it isn't recorded.
Step 3: I assumed each black 2x3 plate goes on the vertical face of one bracket, with the stud side of the face covered. The page does not make clear exactly which bracket each plate sits on.

Step 4: the two curved 2x2 bricks go one on each side of the engine, on the studs of the black 2x3 side plates (b38 and b39). Each gets a sticker (a gauge or screen label), which isn't recorded as a piece.

Step 5: the dark gray side-handle plate (b42) sits on the two top studs of the gray brackets, at the rear. The two black tail fins go on the free studs of the side plates, one on each side. Which fin goes on which plate is assumed. Each fin gets a sticker, which isn't recorded.
I could not see exactly which studs each piece covers. The rests_on lists are my best reading of the page.
Step 6: binoculars go on the handle plate (b42), and the arm goes on the other end of it. The cheese slope goes on the top studs of the bracket, with the black clip tile on top of the slope.
Step 7: the 6L bar with stop ring goes into the clip of the black tile, with the neon-green cone on its front end. The handlebars are held in the second clip of the arm.

Correction to earlier pages. The parts list has only one lego-63965 and two lego-3957a antennas. The posts on pages 2 and 3 have a round top and a flared base, so they are probably the 3957a antennas, not 63965. The earlier ids b2 and b10 should be read as lego-3957a. The bar with stop ring used on this page is the single lego-63965.
The exact studs for the slope and which bar end each piece clips to are assumed from the pictures.

Step 8: the sub-assembly is built first. A dark gray 1x1 tile goes on the stud of the black 1x1 plate with clip, and a sticker (a control panel with dials) goes on the tile. A sticker isn't a piece, so it isn't recorded.
The sub-assembly's clip then snaps onto the handlebars near their stem, where the arrow points. This target is my best reading of the page. It could instead be the end of the arm b48.
Page 13 starts the fourth model. The small picture at the top left shows the finished model, so I did not record it.
Step 1: the sub-assembly shown is the single black cylinder (lego-30360). The reddish-brown round plate goes onto the studs on its end face. I recorded that as a sideways join using the side studs.
Step 2: the axle goes through the plate's axle hole and into the cylinder. The reddish-brown 1x2 plate goes on the top studs of the cylinder. Which studs it covers is assumed.

Step 3: the bracket, grille tile and fin are built as a sub-assembly first. The black grille tile goes on the studs of the bracket's vertical face, and the black tail fin goes on the remaining face studs. A sticker (a small logo) goes on the fin. A sticker isn't a piece, so it isn't recorded.
The finished sub-assembly sits on the top studs of the cylinder and the reddish-brown 1x2 plate (b54 and b57). Which studs each piece covers is my best reading of the page.

Step 4: this is the mirror of page 14's sub-assembly (bracket, grille tile, tail fin). It goes on the opposite side of the cylinder. The fin carries a red stripe sticker, which isn't a piece and isn't recorded.
The bracket sits on the top studs of the cylinder and the reddish-brown plate (b54 and b57). Which studs it covers is my best reading of the page.

Step 5: each dark gray jumper plate goes on the top studs of one gray bracket (b58 and b61). A dark gray 1x1 tile then caps the single stud of each jumper. The light gray cheese slope goes on a top stud of the cylinder at the rear.
The picture is small. Which stud each piece covers is my best reading, and the tiles-on-jumpers placement is assumed.
Step 6: the second reddish-brown round plate goes on the rear end of the cylinder, opposite the front plate b55. The flame's bar end then goes into its axle hole.
This leaves two lego-3957a antennas unplaced on this model. They are the posts used on pages 2 and 3, so the ids b2 and b10 there should be lego-3957a, as noted on page 11.
Step 7: no new pieces. The rocket sub-assembly (cylinder b54 with its fins and flame) is joined to the black engine model (b35) by pushing its axle (b56) into the engine's open end.
The page doesn't show which port of the engine the axle enters, so the join is recorded without a port name.
Step 8: the finished rocket bike with the orange alien minifigure seated on it. No new pieces are added. The minifigure is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded.

The inventory shows element 395726 (2x), a black bar with a round end. This matches the two posts on pages 2 and 3. It is probably lego-3957a. This supports the earlier correction that b2 and b10 are lego-3957a, not lego-63965. The single lego-63965 (element 4538722) is the bar used on page 11.
This page is an advertisement for LEGO Club and the LEGO shop. It has no building steps.
This page is a survey and prize-draw advertisement. It has no building steps.

The two lego-3957a antennas were never placed under that type. The posts on pages 2 and 3 (ids b2 and b10) were recorded as lego-63965, but they are most likely the 3957a antennas, as noted on pages 11 and 22. The bar on page 11 (b51) is the single lego-63965.

Fix for the parts-list mismatch. b2 (stop sign post, page 2) and b10 (traffic light post, page 3) are re-listed with type lego-3957a (Antenna 1 x 4, black). These are the 2x black posts in the inventory (element 395726). They replace the earlier lego-63965 entries for the same ids. Their joins and everything else about them stay the same. This leaves one lego-63965, b51 on page 11, and two lego-3957a. Both counts now match the parts list.

The four separate groups are real, not an error. The booklet builds four independent models: (1) the stop sign, b1 to b3, page 2; (2) the traffic light, b4 to b11, page 3; (3) the Space Police white flyer with the agent, b12 to b34, pages 4 to 8; (4) the orange alien's rocket bike, b35 to b70, pages 9 to 18. Nothing in the booklet joins them. So I did not add any edges between them, to avoid inventing connections.
Within the bike model, the rocket and engine halves are joined by the axle b56 into b35, as recorded on page 18.

Parts-list fix, resent. b2 (stop sign post, page 2) and b10 (traffic light post, page 3) are lego-3957a (Antenna 1 x 4, black), not lego-63965. The inventory shows these as the 2x black posts (element 395726). Each id appears once with this corrected type and replaces its earlier entry. Their joins stay as recorded: b2 in the axle hole of b1, and b10 under b4 and in the axle hole of b11. If the earlier lego-63965 entries for b2 and b10 cannot be overridden, treat their type as lego-3957a. The only true lego-63965 is b51 on page 11. With this fix both counts match the parts list: two lego-3957a, one lego-63965.

The four separate groups are real, not a mistake. The booklet builds four independent models, and no step joins them. (1) The stop sign, b1 to b3, page 2. (2) The traffic light, b4 to b11, page 3. (3) The Space Police white flyer, b12 to b34, pages 4 to 8. (4) The orange alien's rocket bike, b35 to b70, pages 9 to 18. Adding edges between them would invent connections that are not in the booklet, so I kept them as separate models.
